standouts.head: A bull flag
standouts.text: It ran +23% in 14 sessions, then drifted for 6 sessions on lighter volume, giving back 47% of the run: a pause that often precedes the next leg.
standouts.learn: A sharp move (the pole), then a shallow drift on light volume (the flag); the next leg often matches much of the pole.

standouts.head: A smooth, steady uptrend
standouts.text: Over three months price has climbed +40% along a steady line (fit 0.92 of 1): an orderly trend, not a spike.
standouts.learn: How closely price has tracked a straight line; steady trends tend to persist, spikes tend to fade.

standouts.head: Retesting its breakout level
standouts.text: It broke out above the September high and has come back to test it from above: old resistance acting as new support.
standouts.learn: After a breakout, price often comes back to the line it broke; old resistance becomes new support.

standouts.head: Momentum holding a bull range
standouts.text: RSI has stayed above 51 on every dip for three months and reached 81: the range momentum holds in an uptrend.
standouts.learn: In uptrends RSI tends to hold 40 on dips and reach 70; in downtrends it fails near 60 and reaches 30.

standouts.head: Quiet selling on the dip
standouts.text: Volume on the current pullback runs 20% below its 50-day average: profit-taking, not an exit.
standouts.learn: A dip on light volume is profit-taking; a dip on heavy volume is selling.

against.head: Buying is losing force
against.text: Price made a higher high on Oct 14 while 4 of 7 momentum gauges made a lower high (regular bearish divergence).
against.learn: Price makes a higher high but momentum makes a lower high: buyers are tiring.

against.head: A pullback that is not done
against.text: The pullback from the Oct 14 high is not done: it has not reached the 0.5 retracement and it is too quick for the advance before it. A wave 2 usually takes three waves and reaches the 0.618–0.786 of the Feb 25–Oct 14 advance (−29% to −40%).
against.learn: A real wave 2 takes three waves and time, on lighter volume. Too shallow, too quick, one straight leg or rising selling says it has further to go.

VLO.take: VLO: it is in an uptrend on every average, and it sits on support at the September breakout level and the 20-day average. There is a bull flag, and it is in a smooth, steady uptrend. Against it, buying is losing force. The desk is for it.

standouts.head: Wave 2 in its buy zone
standouts.text: Five clean waves up from Mar 30 to Jun 25 (+54%, wave 1). The pullback has reached the 0.618–0.786 zone of that advance (+5.3% to −2.7%), on lighter volume, with the Apr 1 high and the 38.2% retracement of the Aug 5–Oct 23 drop in the same place. The count is wrong under the start of wave 1 (−13%). A daily close above the wave-1 high (+35%) says wave 3 is under way.
standouts.learn: After five waves up, the pullback that usually ends between the 0.618 and 0.786 retracement of the advance. The zone is where to watch; a daily close up inside it is the buy. Under the start of wave 1 the count is wrong.

against.head: Weekly chart: declining
against.text: On the weekly chart price is below a falling 30-week average: the declining stage.
against.learn: Stocks cycle through basing, advancing, topping and declining; the advancing stage (above a rising 30-week average) is where longs pay.

against.head: A lower high and a lower low
against.text: Its last swing high and swing low each came in under the one before.
against.learn: A swing high under the one before and a swing low under the one before: the steps of a downtrend.

against.head: Resistance +2.1% above
against.text: The nearest ceiling is +2.1% above (0.7 ATR), where 7 levels of 4 kinds meet: the Oct 15 high, the 50-week average and the 50% retracement of the Sep 15–Oct 9 drop: little room before sellers have stepped in before.
against.learn: A price area where sellers stepped in before.

VZ.take: VZ: it is below its averages, below resistance at the May 1 high; the buy waits for a daily close above it. Selling is losing force, and it is 14% below its 52-week high. Against it, the weekly chart is in its declining stage. The desk stays out until the trigger's close says otherwise.
VZ.change: No trade until a daily close above +8.8%; once in, a daily close below +5.8%, under the May 1 high, proves it wrong. The case against, that the weekly chart is in its declining stage, fails on a weekly close above +4.6%, the 30-week average.
